title: Naturality of the abelian representable generator
statement: For h:Y→X, W,V in X.Etale and v:V→W, let g:Y×_X V→Y×_X W be its base change and let i:(r_V)* ≅ (r_W)* ⋙ g* be upperStarComp, where r_W and r_V are the projections to Y. The generator defined in [def-sbc-abelian-representable-cohomology-map] satisfies generator(h,V) ≫ (r_V)*.map(h*.map(Z[v])) ≫ i.hom.app(h*Z[W]) = (upperStarConstantSheafIso(g)).inv.app(ULift Z) ≫ g*.map(generator(h,W)). This is an equality of morphisms from the constant abelian sheaf ULift Z on Y×_X V to g*(r_W)*(h*Z[W]), for arbitrary schemes and arbitrary h; no open immersion assumption on W or V is needed.

source.place: Lemma 59.51.6, restriction on the cohomology presheaf; explicit free-sheaf and inverse-image adjunction calculation by X3

proof.text: Identify the constant-sheaf adjunct of the generator with the defining section: invert H.equiv₀ and Ext.addEquiv₀, then evaluate the free ULift Z homomorphism on 1. Write this section as restriction of the inverse-image unit along the final-object identification followed by pullback symmetry.

For arbitrary etale objects r:T→Y and s:S→Y with s=j≫r, compare the inverse-image units with localization restriction. Apply unit_leftAdjointUniq and the composition-unit equation, then identify the iterated-pullback arrows by their two projections. Combining this identity with the constant-section adjunct pullback theorem expresses the adjunct of j* m, transported by upperStarComp inverse, as restriction of the section for m.

Naturality of the sheafification, free-abelian, and ULift Yoneda adjunctions identifies precomposition by the free-representable map of v with section restriction. Apply inverse-image unit naturality to deduce naturality of the section defining the generator. The two arrows into the base-changed etale object agree after both pullback projections, using pullback symmetry and the pullback.map projection equations.

Cancel the inverse upperStarComp component, apply the constant-sheaf hom adjunction and the free-Z hom equivalence injectively, and use the preceding section identities. Naturality of the localization restriction isomorphism and its inverse-hom cancellation finish the equality.

lean.statement:
theorem abelianRepresentableGenerator_coherence {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    (h : Y ⟶ X) (W V : X.Etale) (v : V ⟶ W) :
    let g := pullback.map h V.hom h W.hom (𝟙 Y) v.left (𝟙 X) (by simp) (by simp)
    let i := upperStarComp AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g (pullback.fst h W.hom)
      (pullback.fst h V.hom) (by simp [g])
    abelianRepresentableGenerator h V ≫
        (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} (pullback.fst h V.hom)).map
          ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} h).map ((abelianRepresentable X).map v)) ≫
        i.hom.app ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} h).obj
          ((abelianRepresentable X).obj W)) =
      (Scheme.upperStarConstantSheafIso AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).inv.app
          (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift ℤ)) ≫
        (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} g).map (abelianRepresentableGenerator h W)
